instructions: Pat the 1.5 lb swordfish dry with paper towels. Sprinkle 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper over both sides and leave it on a plate while you prep.
Meanwhile, halve the 2 pints cherry tomatoes and thinly slice the 2 garlic cloves. Slice 1/2 cup of the olives into rings. Rinse and drain 2 tbsp of the capers, and chop 2 tbsp of the parsley.

Set a large skillet over medium heat with no oil and add the 1/4 cup pine nuts. Toast them for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking the pan often, until they're golden and smell toasty. Transfer them to a small bowl. They burn fast, so stay with them.

Turn the heat up to medium high and add 2 tbsp of the olive oil. When it shimmers, lay the swordfish in the pan. Leave it alone for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is golden and lets go of the pan.
Flip the steaks and cook the other side for 1 minute. Move them back to the plate. They'll finish cooking in the sauce.
Turn the heat down to medium and add the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and the garlic. Stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant but hasn't browned.
Add the tomatoes, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the 1 tsp oregano. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes have slumped and their juice has turned into a loose sauce.
Stir in the olives and capers. Nestle the swordfish back into the pan with any juices from the plate and spoon some of the tomatoes over the top.

Cover the pan, turn the heat to medium low and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until the fish is done. You're cooking it to 140°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Push a fork into the thickest part: it's done when it's opaque all the way through and flakes.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Scatter the parsley, the toasted pine nuts and the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper over the top. Serve each steak with the tomatoes and olives spooned over it.
method_notes: All three cook the swordfish in a quick pan sauce of tomatoes, olives and olive oil rather than baking it. GialloZafferano fries a garlic clove in oil, cooks halved cherry tomatoes with oregano for about 10 minutes, adds sliced green olives, then cooks the fish right in the sauce under a lid and tops it with toasted pine nuts. Vincenzo's Plate uses kalamata olives, capers, parsley and chili and steams the steaks in the sauce about 3 1/2 minutes a side; Stefan's Gourmet Blog flours and browns the fish first and builds a canned tomato sauce with onion, anchovy, white wine, capers and black olives. This follows GialloZafferano's sauce and timing, adds the capers the other two use, and gives the fish a short sear first as Stefan does.
